findings.impact: This contradicts the stated checkout/.work replacement refusal, bundle-last publication meaning, portable result binding, and required batch/transport inode-replacement tests. A later pinned inspect would fail closed, but this staging API itself would already have returned a false successful result.
findings.problem: stage_bytes authenticates directory identities only within one file call and closes all descriptors before returning. The proposed API performs several independent calls. Replacing the batch or transaction-inspect directory between successful content calls is accepted as a new safe tree; bundle-last can then publish bundle.json beside only a suffix of the declared content set. The API can return success and an apparently complete manifest although the final layout is incomplete. already_staged aggregation also cannot authenticate one common directory lineage.
findings.required_change: Before freeze, define a multi-file identity boundary. Recommended: narrowly extend staging.py and the implementation path ceiling with an additive authenticated staging session/batch primitive that retains or compares checkout, .work, batch, transaction-inspect and content directory dev/inode identities across the complete ordered write set, then verifies the complete final file set before reporting success. Preserve existing stage_bytes behavior. Alternatively revise the public API to combine staging with mandatory pinned inspection and explicitly make the staging result non-authoritative; that is a larger scope change. Merely calling stage_bytes again cannot provide one atomic lineage and should not be presented as closing this requirement.
